title: German Neonatal Network
summary:
Background: Premature and sick newborns in neonatal intensive care units often have a high risk of long-term health problems. 
Research question: The GNN study collects data and biomaterials from premature and newborn babies from more than 70 neoantal intensive care units throughout Germany. The study center (University of Lübeck) produces annual reports for all participating centers, comparing the data from single units. In addition, the GNN study examines the biosamples using state-of-the-art methods to identify the causes of serious complications in newborns and premature babies.
Methodology: The study collects data from inpatient stays as well as long-term data (e.g., progress after 5–7 or 10–14 years).
conditions: Certain conditions originating in the perinatal period

interventions.name: A multicenter cohort study that includes both sick newborns and preterm infants, as well as healthy newborns serving as control subjects. Data on the premature and newborn infants are collected by the attending physicians during the hospital stay. After discharge, parents receive annual questionnair

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preterm infants born at 28 weeks of gestation or less
Neonates receiving therapeutic hypothermia
Healthy control neonates
Exclusion criteria:
Preterm infants and neonates who were transferred after the first day of life from another hospital to the study site.
